source_findings.finding: All ten conversion names carry one official case-insensitive parameter in the map. Forward names are Inches, Centimeters, Millimeters, Picas and Lines; all reverse names use Points. _wordUnitCall accepts exactly one positional or matching named argument, rejects omission, extra arguments and unknown names, and checks the unwrapped expression's numeric compatibility.

source_findings.area: Evaluation order and once-only argument evaluation
source_findings.finding: Bare and Application member calls select _evaluateWordUnitCall before the generic argument evaluation path. It unwraps a named argument then evaluates its value exactly once through the ordinary work-budget evaluator. Member receiver evaluation still precedes argument evaluation. Scalar helpers and side-effecting helper arguments retain execution ordering.

The five conversion lookups use containsKey and remain guarded by the Word language/application type. Word-only reservation is retained. Checker validation still traverses unused helpers and dead branches. Numeric Variant contents are checked dynamically by _number; Boolean, string, Empty, Null and object values are not implicitly accepted.

The input passes existing finite/common-exact-integer bounds, then is promoted to binary64 before multiplication. Rational factors match 72 points/inch, 12 points/pica or line, and the inferred exact metric ratios 3600/127 and 360/127. Exact inverse equality alone permits native-grid canonicalization; there is no epsilon test. Integer products are bounded before use. Ordinary binary64 rounding can still naturally produce an on-grid result, as the contract states.

PointsToLines retains number / 12 behavior for off-grid scalar fallback via numerator 1, denominator 12. The selected high-range fallback comparisons, including maximum common exact integer, agree in the current-source numeric model.

All retained intentionally invalid named-call fixtures use Value:=, which remains an unknown parameter for all eight new physical methods. They do not conflict with the newly accepted official names. The 17 canonical native cases and all six precision-refusal fixtures agree with the current evaluator model. Both large scalar expectations added in d5 agree within their stated binary64 tolerances. Integration and BAS source continue to target unchanged native APIs.

The incoming Word contract accurately describes positional and official named arguments, actual numeric values, once-only evaluation, the binary64/common-bound model, exact inverse canonicalization, native precision and explicit CLng rounding, and lack of Single subtype/rounding emulation. It expressly distinguishes authored fixtures from unavailable Dart runtime qualification.

The conversion compiler emits scalar values using existing write operations. This review found no new native runtime, serialization, permission, allowlist or publication implementation in the compiler delta.
